# Shiraz

> Shiraz is an open-source (GPL-3.0-only), GTK-free Android compatibility layer that runs supported Android APKs directly on Linux, Apple Silicon macOS (experimental), and Windows (experimental foundation) using standalone ART, SDL2, and native graphics/audio/OS bridges — without booting an Android system image, virtual machine, container, or kernel binder module.

Snapshot version: v0.367.1 (data updated 2026-11-24).

## Core Facts

- **Execution model:** App-only API translation layer on standalone ART (with pre-warmed WarmArtPool standby daemon on Linux and macOS). No Android VM, LXC container, or binder kernel driver.
- **API 35 Java surface:** 4,445 of 4,445 Android 15 / API 35 `android.*` class names present across 49 packages (class-name presence is not CTS certification or full behavioral parity).
- **API 35 NDK C/C++ surface:** 15 of 15 tracked NDK shared libraries built, exporting 887 of 887 cataloged C symbols (audited with `nm`).
- **Host OS backends:**
  - **Linux (x86_64, ARM64 — primary):** Standalone ART, warm standby pool, GBM/DMA-BUF zero-copy swapchain, ALSA/PipeWire AAudio, bundled `libvulkan.so` with real-ICD `PackageManager` probe, default-on Landlock + `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` sandboxing (`--no-sandbox` opt-out, `--no-network`/`--no-internet` seccomp), WebRTC streaming, AppImage & sandboxed Flatpak (`.flatpak`) builders (CLI `--digitalis` ARM64 bundling).
  - **macOS (Apple Silicon ARM64 — experimental port):** 48 verified, 21 partial, 22 open goal checklist items; ART `mach_vm_remap`/`MAP_JIT`/ARM64 fault primitives, wired `WarmArtPool` standby (`2.67×` faster launch on 2048), ANGLE-Metal zero-copy IOSurface swapchain, SurfaceTexture, `MTLSharedEvent` native fences, 120 Hz `CVDisplayLink` vsync, pinned **MoltenVK v1.4.2** (live Metal Vulkan 1.4.357 on Apple M2 Pro across host/guest thunks & Java `PackageManager` `level=1`), VideoToolbox/AudioToolbox, opt-in guest ELF/Bionic loader booting OsmAnd+, F-Droid v2.0.2, Math & Telegram, default-on Seatbelt sandboxing, signed `.app` bundler, and browser `.app` sidecar zip packaging.
  - **Windows (x64, ARM64 — experimental foundation):** 32 verified, 5 partial, 0 open items (CI-verified Win32 primitives, SDL2 presentation/IME/clipboard, DXGI shared AHB, `libvulkan.dll`, WASAPI AAudio/OpenSL ES, Media Foundation decode + `IMFSourceReader` camera capture, DirectWrite, Job Object/Restricted Token sandbox, portable/MSIX bundler; partial foundations for ANGLE-D3D11 Per-Monitor V2 DPI, Win32 ART `NativeBridge` v3 + guest ELF/SysV↔Win64 thunks, and pinned `patches/art-win32-build.patch` + `bootstrap_windows.py` ART orchestrator). Live Win32 `libart.dll` execution remains open.
- **Recorded apps:** 18 apps (17 Partial, 1 Blocked, 0 Historical) across 8 engines (Android framework, Flutter, React Native, Unity, libGDX, Godot, SDL, Arc).
- **Packaging:** Browser-based Go/WASM Builder produces standalone Linux AppImages, sandboxed Flatpak (`.flatpak`) bundles (with Digitalis ARM64 bundling support), and unmodified signed macOS `.app` sidecar zips locally without uploading the APK; CLI also supports `--digitalis` ARM64-on-x86_64 bundling, builds signed macOS `.app` and Windows portable/MSIX bundles, and runs `shiraz install-desktop`.

## Explicit Boundaries (Do Not Misstate)

- Shiraz is experimental. No whole-Android compatibility percentage or CTS certification is claimed.
- Shiraz does **not** include the Google Play Store or Google Play Services.
- OS process sandboxing is enabled by default across `shiraz run`, `shiraz install-desktop`, `shiraz daemon`, Linux AppImages (`--no-sandbox` opt-out, `--no-network`/`--no-internet`), and Flatpak bundles, but this is OS process confinement rather than Android's full per-UID/SELinux sandbox.
- WebView uses an embedded pure-Java HTML5 DOM/JS engine (including interactive `contentEditable`, `Selection`/`Range`, `execCommand`, `MutationObserver`, timers, and DOM storage) rather than a full Blink/V8 browser engine.
- 32-bit ARM (`armeabi-v7a`) native libraries are unsupported; Digitalis ARM64 translation on `x86_64` Linux works in CLI runs and CLI `--digitalis` AppImage/Flatpak builds (not yet in prebuilt browser bases).

## Website Pages

- [Home & Browser Builder](https://spectre-oss.github.io/shiraz/): Architecture overview, Shiraz Web (WebRTC), macOS Launcher, and in-browser AppImage/Flatpak APK packager.
- [Run APK in Browser](https://spectre-oss.github.io/shiraz/run/): 100% client-side in-browser Android APK runner powered by Shiraz (aarch64 Linux runtime) inside [pithings/unkernel](https://github.com/pithings/unkernel) (Linux 7.3 + kwemu on WebAssembly). Zero backend compute.
- [Compatibility & Coverage Tracker](https://spectre-oss.github.io/shiraz/compatibility/): Filterable app compatibility catalog, 3-OS host matrix, 30 subsystem notes, 49-package API 35 breakdown, 15-library NDK audit, and behavioral probe tracker.
- [Compare Shiraz and Its Peers](https://spectre-oss.github.io/shiraz/compare/): Side-by-side comparison with ATL, ACL, a4l, Mac.apk, apklayer, Innkeeper, Waydroid, and Android Emulator.
- [Full AI Context (llms-full.txt)](https://spectre-oss.github.io/shiraz/llms-full.txt): Complete single-file reference with app records, host layers, subsystem limits, and FAQs.

## Documentation & Source

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz): GPL-3.0-only source code, releases, and issue tracker.
- [Tested Applications](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/tested.md): Observed app walkthroughs and open limits.
- [Cross-Platform Architecture](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/cross_platform.md): Linux, macOS, and Windows host layer summary.
- [Framework APIs Goal](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/framework_final_goal.md): All 4,445 Android API 35 classes across 49 areas.
- [NDK Libraries Goal](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/ndk_final_goal.md): All 15 tracked API 35 NDK libraries (887 symbols).
- [macOS Native Goal](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/macos_final_goal.md): Apple Silicon checklist and OsmAnd+ walkthrough notes.
- [Windows Native Goal](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/windows_final_goal.md): Win32/DXGI/WASAPI/MSIX checklist and CI coverage.
- [Browser Builder Guide](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/BUILDER.md): Client-side Go/WASM AppImage and Flatpak assembly.
- [Shiraz Web Guide](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/docs/WEB.md): Streaming apps over WebRTC to any browser or Linux phone.
- [Security Model](https://github.com/spectre-oss/shiraz/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Isolation boundaries and safe testing guidance.
